case_name: Rachamreddi Chenna Reddy and Others v State of Andhra Pradesh
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

9 February 1999
Cr.A. No. 767 of 1991 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 17 September 1987 of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in Cr. A. No. 941 of 1986)
The Judgment was delivered by: PATTANAIK, J.
1.  The appellants and two
facts: The appellants and two others, in all ten in number, stood charged and were tried for having committed the offence under Section 302/149, 307/149 and 148 Indian Penal Code...

There was some dispute six months prior to the date of occurrence between the prosecution party and the accused party on account of the fact that PW 1, who is the brother of the two deceased person, obstructed the passage to the house do Accused 1 to 3.
A week prior to the date of occurrence there had been an alternation between the two faction on account of some theft having taken having taken place.
On the date occurrence on 10-12-1985 PW 1 went to the house of his brother who is one of deceased in the case and both of them went together to their field.

By 12.00 noon while they were returning and PW 1 was following his deceased brother, in front of the flour mill in the village the accused persons came armed with lethal weapons and Accused 1 hacked the deceased with a sickle right on the road.
Nine other accused persons then surrounded the deceased and attacked him with their respective weapons in their hands.
PW 1 started running from the place to save his life and the accused persons also tried to chase him but could not catch hold of him.
The accused persons then came back and proceeded to the second place of occurrence where PW 3 and the second deceased were returning.
PW 3 went and informed PW 1 who was by that time near the dead body of the first deceased.
PW 1 in the company of PW 3 came to the second place of occurrence which was nearby and then a complaint was drafted by PW 5 on the basis of information given by PW 1.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: He relied on the decision of this Court in Anil Phukan v. State of Assam (1993 Indlaw SC 403) and contended that the evidence of PWs 1, 3 and 4 is not of such unimpeachable character relying upon which the courts could have convicted these appellants of the charge under Sections 302/149.

He also contended that in any view of the matter the prosecution has failed to establish the ingredients of S. 149 and the conviction of the appellants by taking recourse to S. 149 cannot be sustained.
He relied upon the decisions of this Court in the case of Bolineedi Venkataramaiah v. State of A.P., Thakore Dolji Vanvirji v. State of Gujarat (1992 Indlaw SC 70 : 1992 Indlaw SC 70).
court_reasoning: The learned Sessions Judge and the High Court scrutinised the evidence of 3 main eyewitnesses of the occurrence, PWs 1, 3 and 4, and held them to be fully reliable and, accordingly, convicted the accused persons.
In our considered opinion, that can hardly be a ground to discard their version.
On re-examining the evidence of the aforesaid witnesses we do not find anything elicited in their cross-examination to impeach their testimony.
The Court has also further held that mere relationship of the witness with the deceased is no ground to discard his testimony if it is otherwise found to be reliable.

In Bolineedi case (1993 Indlaw SC 962) this Court held that for arriving at a conclusion of constructive liability, what the courts have to see is whether they had the common object and members of the assembly knew it likely to be committed in prosecution of that object.
holding: The conviction of the appellants by taking recourse to S. 149 cannot be sustained.
The Court has also further held that mere relationship of the witness with the deceased is no ground to discard his testimony if it is otherwise found to be reliable.
The judgment of the learned Sessions Judge as affirmed by the High Court in appeal is fully justified.
